notes: GAPS / LOW-CONFIDENCE ITEMS: (1) APTEL Chairperson position is vacant since ~August 2025 per Wikipedia's chairperson table; the official aptel.gov.in 'Chairperson' page shows no current occupant, which is consistent with (but not an independent confirmation of) the vacancy. (2) SAT (Securities Appellate Tribunal) presiding officer 'Justice Dinesh Kumar' is sourced only from an undated Wikipedia line; sat.gov.in returned HTTP 503 throughout this research session and could not be reached to verify. Flagged low confidence — needs re-check. (3) NCDRC President 'Justice Amreshwar Pratap Sahi' is Wikipedia-sourced 'as of 2024'; ncdrc.nic.in is a client-side-rendered SPA that could not be scraped statically to confirm he is still President as of 2026-09-25. (4) CAT (Central Administrative Tribunal)'s administering ministry is inferred as the Department of Personnel & Training (given DoPT's historical role in constituting CAT for central-govt service matters); no single authoritative source confirmed this explicitly — cgat.gov.in is also a client-rendered SPA. (5) Exact current bench counts for NCLT (Wikipedia cites 16 physical benches across 15 official site locations, with some ambiguity) and ITAT (zonal structure documented via 8 Vice-President zones, but no single total-bench figure found) are approximate. (6) NCLAT Chairperson 'Justice Yogesh Khanna' is confirmed CURRENT (officiating) via live nclat.nic.in bench notices dated Sept 2026, but the exact date he assumed the officiating chairpersonship was not found (only his 2024-02-19 date of joining as a Judicial Member). (7) Railway Claims Tribunal and Central Government Industrial Tribunals-cum-Labour Courts (CGIT) are structurally decentralised (each bench/tribunal has its own presiding officer) so no single national 'holder' Position was created for them — this matches the pattern used for DRT/DRAT. CGIT's exact current count of tribunals could not be verified: labour.gov.in / clc.gov.in are Next.js client-rendered sites that returned only empty app shells to non-browser fetches (curl/WebFetch), and this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before this could be resolved another way. (8) Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021 abolished several appellate bodies entirely (Cinematograph Appellate Tribunal, Trade Marks Appellate Board, Copyright Appellate Board, Customs Authority for Advance Rulings, Patents Appellate Board, Airport Appellate Tribunal, National Highways Appellate Tribunal, Geographical Indications Appellate Board), shifting their jurisdiction to High Courts / Commercial Courts / civil courts / the Central Government — per PRS Legislative Research's bill summary. These are NOT included as entities since they no longer exist. (9) This session's WebSearch tool quota was exhausted almost immediately (shared across parallel research agents), so all research after the first few queries relied on curl (Wikipedia parse API + official *.gov.in/*.nic.in sites) and WebFetch; several official tribunal sites (cgat.gov.in, ncdrc.nic.in, drt.gov.in, labour.gov.in, doj.gov.in) are JavaScript single-page apps that return an empty shell to non-browser HTTP clients and could not be scraped for current office-holder data beyond what is noted above. VERIFICATION PASS (2026-09-25) ADDITIONS: investigated whether the Appellate Tribunal under SAFEMA/PMLA/FEMA/NDPS (a.k.a. Appellate Tribunal for Forfeited Property) should be added as a 17th entity -- it is a real, distinct central tribunal not in the original 16 -- but could not find a live official source (dor.gov.in candidate URL 404'd) or a reliable 2025-2026 source for its current chairperson within this session's tool budget (WebSearch quota was exhausted session-wide before this could be resolved). NOT added, to avoid inventing a chairperson name or stale legal-basis text -- flagged here as a known coverage gap for a follow-up research pass.

entities.name: National Green Tribunal
entities.description: Specialised statutory tribunal for expeditious disposal of civil cases involving substantial questions relating to protection of environment and natural resources, and for providing relief and compensation for damages to persons and property from environmental harm.

entities.name: National Company Law Tribunal
entities.description: Quasi-judicial body adjudicating company-law matters: insolvency resolution and liquidation of companies/LLPs under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016, oppression and mismanagement, mergers, amalgamations and winding-up of companies.
entities.legalBasis: Companies Act, 2013 (Section 408); also functions as Adjudicating Authority under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

stats.note: Wikipedia (2021-era update) described 16 physical benches across these cities (Delhi hosting multiple); exact current per-city bench count not independently re-confirmed.

entities.name: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal
entities.description: Appellate tribunal hearing appeals against NCLT orders (including IBC insolvency/liquidation matters) and against orders/directions of the Competition Commission of India and the National Financial Reporting Authority. Its orders are appealable to the Supreme Court.

entities.name: Income Tax Appellate Tribunal
entities.description: Second appellate authority under the direct-tax statutes and the first independent forum in the direct-tax appellate hierarchy; its orders are final except where a substantial question of law arises for the High Court.
entities.legalBasis: Income-tax Act, 1961 (Section 252); originally constituted 1941 under the Income Tax Act, 1922 (Section 5A)

stats.note: Exact current total bench count not independently re-confirmed in this research pass; ITAT began in 1941 with 3 benches (Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai) and has expanded substantially since.

entities.name: Central Administrative Tribunal
entities.description: Adjudicates disputes and complaints relating to recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to central public services and posts (and some state government employees under specified arrangements), functioning with powers similar to a High Court in its own contempt proceedings.

stats.note: 1 Chairman + up to 34 Judicial + 35 Administrative members per Wikipedia; cgat.gov.in is a client-rendered site and could not be independently scraped to corroborate this figure.

entities.name: Armed Forces Tribunal
entities.description: Military tribunal adjudicating disputes and complaints on service and conditions of service of Army, Navy and Air Force personnel, and hearing appeals from orders, findings or sentences of courts-martial.

stats.note: Principal Bench (Delhi) plus 10 regional benches per Wikipedia.

entities.name: Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal
entities.description: Quasi-judicial body hearing appeals against orders passed under the Customs Act 1962 and Central Excise Act 1944 (and, for the pre-GST period, service tax under the Finance Act 1994); also has appellate jurisdiction in anti-dumping matters against orders of the Designated Authority in the Ministry of Commerce.
entities.legalBasis: Customs Act, 1962 (Section 129), as amended by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 1980 and Finance Act, 2003

entities.name: Appellate Tribunal for Electricity
entities.description: Statutory and autonomous body hearing appeals against orders of the Central and State Electricity Regulatory Commissions and the adjudicating officer under the Electricity Act; since 2007 also the appellate forum for orders of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB). Second appeal on substantial questions of law lies to the Supreme Court.

entities.name: Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal
entities.description: Adjudicates disputes between telecom service providers and between service providers and consumers, and hears appeals against directions, decisions or orders of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI); also has jurisdiction over broadcasting and cable services disputes.
entities.legalBasis: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997 (as amended by the TRAI (Amendment) Act, 2000)

entities.name: Securities Appellate Tribunal
entities.description: Hears appeals against orders passed by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) and the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).
entities.legalBasis: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 (Section 15K)

entities.name: National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
entities.description: Apex quasi-judicial body of India's three-tier consumer-dispute-redressal system; entertains complaints above the top pecuniary threshold and exercises appellate and revisional jurisdiction over State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions.
entities.legalBasis: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (originally constituted 1988 under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986)

stats.note: President + 9 other members, per Wikipedia 'as of 2024'.

entities.name: Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunals
entities.description: Appellate tier hearing appeals against orders of the Debts Recovery Tribunals on recovery of debts owed to banks and financial institutions, and enforcement actions under the SARFAESI Act. 5 DRATs function across India, each headed by its own Chairperson (retired/serving High Court judge) — no single national head.
entities.legalBasis: Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993 (RDB Act); Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest (SARFAESI) Act, 2002

entities.name: Debts Recovery Tribunals
entities.description: First-tier tribunals for expeditious adjudication of claims by banks and financial institutions for recovery of debts, and for related enforcement matters under the SARFAESI Act. 39 DRTs function across India, each headed by its own Presiding Officer — no single national head.
entities.legalBasis: Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993 (RDB Act, formerly the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993)

entities.name: Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal
entities.description: Second appellate authority for GST disputes, hearing appeals against orders of Appellate/Revisional authorities under Sections 107/108 of the CGST Act and corresponding State GST Acts; became operational with e-filing and a Principal Bench plus State Benches during 2025-26, with its e-Journal reporting judgements up to end-August 2026.
entities.legalBasis: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (Section 109)

stats.operationalStatus2025_26: Operational — GSTAT Procedure Rules 2025 and Anti-Profiteering Procedure Rules 2025 notified; e-Filing portal live; e-Journal reporting judgements through 2026-08-31.

entities.name: Railway Claims Tribunal
entities.description: Adjudicates claims for compensation for death or injury to rail passengers, and for loss, destruction, damage, deterioration or non-delivery of goods/parcels/luggage carried by the railways; each bench has its own Chairman/Members — no single national head.

stats.note: Site notice (Feb 2026) says the Tribunal is migrating its case-filing system to https://erct.gov.in

entities.name: Central Government Industrial Tribunals-cum-Labour Courts
entities.description: Adjudicate industrial disputes referred by the Central Government under the Industrial Disputes Act for establishments in the central sphere (railways, banks, ports, mines, major PSUs, etc.); administered through the office of the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central). No single national head — each CGIT-cum-LC is headed by its own Presiding Officer.

holder.name: Justice Prakash Shrivastava
holder.notes: Retired judge, Supreme Court of India. Appointed on the recommendation of a selection committee under the NGT Act.

holder.name: Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal
holder.notes: Retired Chief Justice, later judge of a High Court. Per official NCLT site, tenure runs 2026-05-11 to 2031-03-09. Supersedes earlier President Justice R. Sudhakar (in office since 2021-11-01 per stale Wikipedia data).

Succeeded Justice Tarun Agarwala, whose SAT term ran 2018-12-31 to 2023-12-30 (per Tarun Agarwala's Wikipedia bio, which explicitly names 'P. S. Dinesh Kumar' as successor). Exact appointment date within 2024 not found -- 'since' left at year granularity. sat.gov.in returned HTTP 503 on every fetch attempt across this and the prior research session (site appears down, not just JS-rendered), so the official source remains unconfirmed; corroboration here is cross-referenced Wikipedia biographical pages rather than an official primary source. Original record's 'Justice Dinesh Kumar' (no since-date, generic Economic-Times citation from 2013) was almost certainly a stale/incomplete name for the SAME person now more fully identified as P. S. Dinesh Kumar -- not a different, unconfirmed individual.
